# Problem 1

"We had not selected FSC and SSC parameters in this attempt, as they are normally displayed in the linear scale. Include them in the list of fluorophores to be transformed, and see how this impacts the visualization (imitating what could accidentally happen in practice if they were left in)."


## solution

### code:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE


# set up directory:
getwd()

# activate libraries:
#library(flowWorkspace) 
#library(ggcyto)
#library(dplyr)
#library(stringr)
#library(ggplot2)
#library(flowCore)


# load fcs files
folder_path = file.path("data")
fcs_files= list.files(folder_path, pattern=".fcs", full.names = TRUE)
fcs_files


# sort the different types of files into their respective type of files. 

## Mass cytometry start with G1_2 and spectral flow cytometry files start with 2025.
MC_files=fcs_files[str_detect(fcs_files, "G1_2")]
MC_files

SFC_files=fcs_files[str_detect(fcs_files, "2025")]
SFC_files

# Initialize gatingset for spectral flow cytometry files:
##get files into a cytoset
SFC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(SFC_files, truncate_max_range=FALSE, transformation=FALSE)


## pass files to a gatingset
SFC_gatingset = GatingSet(SFC_cytoset)
SFC_gatingset

# getting metadata from gatingset:
metadata = pData(SFC_gatingset)
metadata

# create new columns to add to metadata by extracting condition data and specimen name data
TwoExtraColumns = metadata |> mutate(Condition = name) |>
     mutate(Condition=str_extract(Condition, "[^_]+(?=\\.fcs$)")) |>
     mutate(Specimen=str_extract(name, "INF\\d{3}")) |> select(Condition, Specimen)
TwoExtraColumns

# bind two different daat frames together using cbind:
UpdatedMetadata <- cbind(metadata, TwoExtraColumns)
UpdatedMetadata

# update metadata in gatingset:
pData(SFC_gatingset) <- UpdatedMetadata

# getting parameters from gatingset:
SFC_parameters = colnames(SFC_gatingset)
SFC_parameters

# Before transformation is applied:


# plot 1: FSC-A  vs SSC-A for 1 file:
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root",
 aes(x="FSC-A", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

# plot 2: FSC-A vs FCS-W for 1 file (usually a plot for doublets):
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root",
 aes(x="FSC-A", y="FSC-W")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

# plot 3: SSC-A vs Time for 1 file
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root", aes(x="Time", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)


#preparing bioexponential transformation with default values:
Biexponential = flowjo_biexp_trans()

#or
#Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144,pos=4.5, neg=0, widthBasis=-10) 

#applying transformation values to all parameters including scatter and time by creating a transformer list:
MyBiexTransform = transformerList(SFC_parameters, Biexponential)

#  apply the transformation to gating set by rewriting the original gatingset:
transform(SFC_gatingset, MyBiexTransform)

# plot 4: FSC-A  vs SSC-A for 1 file:
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root",
 aes(x="FSC-A", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

# plot 5: FSC-A vs FCS-W for 1 file (usually a plot for doublets):
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root",
 aes(x="FSC-A", y="FSC-W")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

# plot 6: SSC-A vs Time for 1 file
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root", aes(x="Time", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)
```

# Problem 2

"For the SFC data, I showed the setup for both Logicle and Biexponential, but didn’t have time to dive into the Logicle transformation. Select a couple markers of interest for the SFC data, visualize and screenshot the before, and then attempt to customize the biexponential arguments to best visualize the underlying data, and then repeat for Logicle. Take screenshots of both and compare/contrast the difference."

## Solution

### code setup:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE


# set up directory:
getwd()

# activate libraries:
#library(flowWorkspace)
#library(ggcyto)
#library(dplyr)
#library(stringr)
#library(ggplot2)
#library(flowCore)


# load fcs files
folder_path = file.path("data")
fcs_files= list.files(folder_path, pattern=".fcs", full.names = TRUE)
fcs_files


# sort the different types of files into their respective type of files. 
# Mass cytometry start with G1_2 and spectral flow cytometry files start with 2025.
MC_files=fcs_files[str_detect(fcs_files, "G1_2")]
MC_files

SFC_files=fcs_files[str_detect(fcs_files, "2025")]
SFC_files

# Initialize gatingset for spectral flow cytometry files:
##get files into a cytoset
SFC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(SFC_files, truncate_max_range=FALSE, transformation=FALSE)


## pass files to a gatingset
SFC_gatingset = GatingSet(SFC_cytoset)
SFC_gatingset

# getting parameters from gatingset:
SFC_parameters = colnames(SFC_gatingset)
SFC_parameters

# removing scatters and time parameters from SFC_parameters for later transformation:
fluorophores_only = SFC_parameters[!str_detect(SFC_parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
fluorophores_only

# getting the marker list to know what I want to plot next:
marker_fluorophores = markernames(SFC_gatingset)
marker_fluorophores
```

### Biexponential transformation examples: 

I want to visualize CD4 BUV-805 vs CD25 PE-Fire 744:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

#preparing bioexponential transformation:
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans() #default values
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144,pos=4.5, neg=0, widthBasis=-1000) # width at -1000
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144/2,pos=4.5, neg=0, widthBasis=-1000) # width and maxvalue changed:



#applying transformation values to  fluorophores_only list by creating a transformer list:
MyBiexTransform <- transformerList(fluorophores_only, Biexponential)

#  apply the transformation to gating set:
transform(SFC_gatingset, MyBiexTransform)

# plot the flow plot for one file:
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root",
 aes(x="BUV805-A", y="PE-Fire 744-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

# confirming the transformation is applied according to what we actually set it to using another sample from our gating set and confirm values for channelrange, maxvalue, neg, pos, ad width basis are the same as the ones we provided.

gh_get_transformations(SFC_gatingset[[1]])$'BUV805-A'
```

### Logical transformation examples:
I want to visualize CD4 BUV-805 vs CD25 PE-Fire 744 but now with logicle transformation.

let's first setup the gating set and the original plot with logicle transformation:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

SFC_files=fcs_files[str_detect(fcs_files, "2025")]
SFC_files

# Initialize gatingset for spectral flow cytometry files:
##get files into a cytoset
SFC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(SFC_files, truncate_max_range=FALSE, transformation=FALSE)


## pass files to a gatingset
SFC_gatingset = GatingSet(SFC_cytoset)
SFC_gatingset

# getting parameters from gatingset:
SFC_parameters = colnames(SFC_gatingset)
SFC_parameters

# removing scatters and time parameters from SFC_parameters for later transformation:
fluorophores_only = SFC_parameters[!str_detect(SFC_parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
fluorophores_only
```

Let's find out what arguments takes the logicle transformation by writing this on the console:

?logicle_trans()
?logicle_transform()

The logicle_trans is, like the flowjo_biexp_trans(), a wrapper function and passes arguments to logicle_transform().

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem2_logicle_help.PNG)


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

#preparing logicle transformation using default values:

Logicle_default = logicle_trans(w = 0.5, t = 262144,
                 m = 4.5, a = 0) #default values

# logicle with t= 10000
Logicle_set1 = logicle_trans(w = 0.5, t = 10000, m=4.5, a=0)

Logicle_set2 = logicle_trans(w = 1, t = 262144, m=4.5, a=0)

Logicle_set3 = logicle_trans(w = 1.5, t = 262144, m=4.5, a=0)

Logicle_set4 = logicle_trans(w = 1.5, t = 262144, m=5, a=0)


#applying transformation values to  fluorophores_only list by creating a transformer list:
My_logicle_transform = transformerList(fluorophores_only, Logicle_set4)

#  apply the transformation to gating set:
transform(SFC_gatingset, My_logicle_transform)

# plot the flow plot for one file:
ggcyto(SFC_gatingset[6], subset="root",
 aes(x="BUV805-A", y="PE-Fire 744-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

# confirming the transformation is applied according to what we actually set it to using another sample from our gating set and confirm values for channelrange, maxvalue, neg, pos, ad width basis are the same as the ones we provided.

gh_get_transformations(SFC_gatingset[[1]])$'BUV805-A'
```

default logicle:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem2_logicle_default.png)


t = 10000

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem2_logicle_1.png)

with logicle transformation it looks like there are extra negative values that are separated.

getting solved with w = 1:

logicle_trans(w = 1, t = 262144, m=4.5, a=0)

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem2_logicle_2.png)


looking better at w= 1.5:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem2_logicle_3.png)


between w =1 and w = 1.5 the plot collapsed too much:

Let's try w= 1.5 and m = 5:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem2_logicle_4.png)

The final plot looks similar to 

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem2_biexponential_2.png)

I think I like how round the population in CD4 is compared to biexponential plot but I also think that for a final plot I'd choose biexponential as the positive and negative events look more balanced in the plot.


# Problem 3

"There are to asinh style transformations provided by the flowWorkspace package. Using the mass cytometry data, select two metal markers of interest, visualize each, customize the arguments until you have properly visualized the underlying populations, and see if you can spot any major differences between the methods."

## Solution

### setup

I will first get the working directory, activate needed libraries, get the full paths to the files and create a gating set for the mass cytometry files I have.

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE 

# activate libraries:
library(flowWorkspace) 
library(ggcyto)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(flowCore)

# load all fcs files
folder_path = file.path("data")

fcs_files = list.files(folder_path, pattern=".fcs", full.names = TRUE)

fcs_files

# sort the different types of files into their respective type of files. 
## Mass cytometry start with G1_2 and spectral flow cytometry files start with 2025.
MC_files = fcs_files[str_detect(fcs_files, "G1_2")]

MC_files

# create a cytoset for mass cytometry files:

MC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(MC_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)

# create a gatingset for MC files:

MC_gatingset = GatingSet(MC_cytoset)
MC_gatingset

# checking names for the metaltags:

metal_tags = colnames(MC_gatingset)
metal_tags

# checking corresponding markers
## calling them marker tags as in markers corresponding to the metal tags
MC_parameters = markernames(MC_gatingset)
MC_parameters
```


After having created the gatingset and get information on which metal tags and markers correspond to those are in variables we can go ahead and try plot using ggcyto().

I want to plot CD14 vs CD16. 

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE


# original plot without transformation applied:

ggcyto(MC_gatingset[1], subset = "root", aes (x ="CD14", y="CD16")) + geom_hex(bins=100) 

# or this code
# ggcyto(MC_gatingset[1], subset = "root", aes (x ="Tb159Di", y="Er167Di")) + geom_hex(bins=100)
# markers can be named by their marker name or by their parameter (fluorochrome or metal) 
```

this is what it looks like without applying transformations:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_1.png)


Let's apply transformation to the parameters of interest. According to this page <https://rdrr.io/bioc/flowWorkspace/man/transform.html> the flowWorkspace library has 2 asinh transforms:

1. flowjo_fasinh_trans, which is a wrapper function for the actual flowjo_fasinh() function

and

2. asinhtGml2_trans(), which in turn is a wrapper function for the actual asinh_Gml2() function.


Starting with the 1st asinh transform where the default values can be gathered from "?flowjo_fasinh": 

## Default values for flowjo_fasinh

flowjo_fasinh(m = 4, t = 12000, a = 0.7, length = 256)
flowjo_fsinh(m = 4, t = 12000, a = 0.7, length = 256)


## arguments:

Arguments
m	
numeric the full width of the transformed display in asymptotic decades

t	
numeric the maximum value of input data

a	
numeric Additional negative range to be included in the display in asymptotic decades

length	
numeric the maximum value of transformed data

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# Remove beads and barcodes from markers of interest.

markers_interest = MC_parameters[!str_detect("Barcode|Beads|beads", MC_parameters)]
markers_interest

# take only the names of the metals those are the ones we will transform

metal_tags = names(markers_interest)
metal_tags


# use asinh to transform the parameters:

## atribute the transform function to a variable:

asinh = flowjo_fasinh_trans() # default values

## transform the paramenter with transformersList:
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, asinh)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])


## apply transformed parameters to the gating set:

transform(MC_gatingset, my_asinh_transform)

# plot with transformation applied:

ggcyto(MC_gatingset[1], subset = "root", aes (x ="CD14", y="CD16")) + geom_hex(bins=100) 
```

plot with default flowjo_fasinh_trans() applied:
![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_2.png)


Let's look at the default values for the other asinh function: "?asinh_Gml2"

## default values for asinh gml2 function 

asinh_Gml2(T = 262144, M = 4.5, A = 0, inverse = FALSE)

## arguments for asinh_gml2():
Arguments
T	
numeric the maximum value of input data

M	
numeric the full width of the transformed display in asymptotic decades

A	
numeric Additional negative range to be included in the display in asymptotic decades

inverse	
whether to return the inverse function


Before we apply the new transform we need to reset the gatingset:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# create a cytoset for mass cytometry files:
MC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(MC_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
# create a gatingset for MC files:
MC_gatingset = GatingSet(MC_cytoset)
MC_gatingset
```

Using gml2 fasinh function:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE


# use asinh to transform the parameters:
## atribute the transform function to a variable:
gml2_fasinh = asinhtGml2_trans() # default values

## transform the paramenter with transformersList:
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, gml2_fasinh)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])


## apply transformed parameters to the gating set:

transform(MC_gatingset, my_asinh_transform)

# plot with transformation applied:

ggcyto(MC_gatingset[1], subset = "root", aes (x ="CD14", y="CD16")) + geom_hex(bins=100) 
```
here's how it looks with gml2 fasinh transformation with default values.

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_3.png)

None of the default transformations looks good, so let's change some parameters in the flowjo_fasinh transform:


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# reset gating set
## create a cytoset for mass cytometry files:
MC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(MC_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
## create a gatingset for MC files:
MC_gatingset = GatingSet(MC_cytoset)
MC_gatingset

# use asinh to transform the parameters:
## atribute the transform function to a variable:
asinh_set1 = flowjo_fasinh_trans(m = 5, t = 12000, a = 0.7, length = 256) # m = 5
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, asinh_set1)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])


asinh_set2 = flowjo_fasinh_trans(m = 4, t = 12000, a = 1, length = 256) # a = 1
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, asinh_set2)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])


asinh_set3 = flowjo_fasinh_trans(m = 5, t = 12000/2, a= 0.7, length = 256) # t=12000/2
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, asinh_set3)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])


asinh_set4 = flowjo_fasinh_trans(m = 5, t = 12000/2, a= 0.3, length = 256) # t=12000/2
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, asinh_set4)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])

## apply transformed parameters to the gating set:

transform(MC_gatingset, my_asinh_transform)

# plot with transformation applied:

ggcyto(MC_gatingset[1], subset = "root", aes (x ="CD14", y="CD16")) + geom_hex(bins=100) 
```

m = 5 (width in asymptotic decades, originally 4)

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_4.png)

looks ok with more decades added to the display.

a = 1 (number of additional negative decades)

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_5.png)

I thought increasing this number would show better the negative populations.

t = 12000/2 (m=5 as well) which is input data

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_6.png)

I like the last plot but I want to see what happens if I decrease a to 0.3

Let's try a new transformation with m = 5, a = 0.3, t= 12000/2:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_7.png)

It collapsed the negative events of CD16 more than the previous one.

Let's try changing the other function default values:


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
# reset gating set
## create a cytoset for mass cytometry files:
MC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(MC_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
## create a gatingset for MC files:
MC_gatingset = GatingSet(MC_cytoset)
MC_gatingset

# use asinh to transform the parameters:
## atribute the transform function to a variable:
gml2fasinh_set1 = asinhtGml2_trans(T = 262144, M = 5, A = 0) # M = 5
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, gml2fasinh_set1)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])

gml2fasinh_set2= asinhtGml2_trans(T = 262144, M = 4, A = 0) # A = 3
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, gml2fasinh_set2)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])

gml2fasinh_set3= asinhtGml2_trans(T = 262144/2, M = 4 , A = 0) # T = 262144/2
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, gml2fasinh_set3)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])

gml2fasinh_set4= asinhtGml2_trans(T = 262144*2, M = 6 , A = -2) 
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, gml2fasinh_set4)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])

gml2fasinh_set5= asinhtGml2_trans(T = 262144*2.5, M = 6.5 , A = -4) # T = 262144/2
my_asinh_transform = transformerList(metal_tags, gml2fasinh_set5)
str(my_asinh_transform[1:3])


## apply transformed parameters to the gating set:

transform(MC_gatingset, my_asinh_transform)

# plot with transformation applied:

ggcyto(MC_gatingset[1], subset = "root", aes (x ="CD14", y="CD16")) + geom_hex(bins=100) 
```


M = 5:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_8.png)

not a lot of improvement, the flowjo_fasinh() had more changes to the better with the similar argument.

A = 3:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_9.png)

it seems like events were lost from the previous plot to this one. No improvement on visualization at all.

T = default/2:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_10.png)

this continues to not be good for visualization.

Let's go on the opposite direction for T and A and increase M a bit more, T = default*2, M = 6, A = -2:

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_11.png)

we are getting somewhere!

T = 262144*2.5, M = 6.5 , A = -4

![](/course/07_Transformations/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_plot_12.png)

The gml2 function took longer to tweak to an ok level compared to the flowjo_fasinh().

The major difference I noticed is how t and T which are similar arguments behaved differently, so t had to decrease to be able to start showing the populations while in the second T had to slightly more than double its value to show the populations properly.

In the description found through research on the internet the main difference between these is:

"It is simply a special form of flowjo_fasinh with length set to 1 and different default values for parameters t,m,a."
